title: Dizi
summary: The dizi is the Chinese side-blown bamboo flute. It has six finger holes and a further hole covered with a thin membrane, which makes the tone bright and slightly buzzing.
howToPlay: Each pipe shows the finger holes to cover: dark discs are covered, light ones left open.
Each mark that falls onto the line is one note; sound that pipe as it arrives and hold the longer ones.
Notes are named in the numbered way: 5 6 7 are the low notes, 1 2 3 the middle ones, then the octave above.
rules: Covering all six holes sounds the lowest note and lifting fingers from the bottom upward climbs the scale; the same fingering sounds an octave higher with a stronger breath.
The three tunes are played twice, in four beats to the bar: a slow scale, a folk-song style tune and a quick run.
A note on the beat scores in full, a close one scores less, and an extra stroke costs a little.
heritageNote: The dizi has been played in China for many centuries in folk music, theatre and village bands, and in two main schools: a lyrical southern style with short ornaments and a fast, bright northern one. Its membrane hole is a distinguishing feature of the instrument.
